Missing a chat or message offer no longer sets an agent to Not ready; only a missed call does. Emails look professional: a clean layout that works in Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail, a properly sized logo, a signature block and a footer, and replies quote the customer's earlier message. Quick replies can fill in {{conversation.reference}} (the ticket number, or a short conversation reference), and the desk warns before sending a message that still has a [fill-in] in square brackets.

Queues and mailboxes warn when nobody can be offered their email (for example, no agent has the queue's skill). Email senders rules say clearly that they act on who sent the email; one of your own mailbox addresses is refused there, with a pointer to the mailbox's Agents' queue.

People at a customer: a business customer lists the people who deal with you, each with a role and their own numbers and emails. Add people, numbers and emails from the customer page (agents for the customer they are handling; supervisors for any). Calls and messages from a person's number show "Thandi Mokoena (Accounts) at Acme Ltd". An unknown caller can be linked to a customer from the desk. The history shows the whole account or one person. BMS contacts become people.

BMS: the full callout history is brought in from BMS; open callouts first, each with its visits. Raise a callout from a call, an email, WhatsApp, SMS or chat, a ticket, or the customer page; supervisors can raise them from the console. The customer page has Call and Message beside each number, the customer's equipment, and orders and deliveries (read only; blank if BMS does not answer). The card says when BMS was last checked (every 15 minutes).

Ticket settings: ready-made categories (with service levels) and resolution codes for every industry: Start from a template. Nothing you set up is changed.

New messages: agents and supervisors can start an SMS, WhatsApp or email. On the desk, New message beside New call and on a customer's record; in the console on the Floor and Customers, choosing where replies go.

Call menus: callers who press nothing can have their own message and route. Transfers and conferences on the desk take numbers as people type them (076…, 2776…, 00…). Floor: "I'm on it" shows who took a request for help."}
